findings.text: `exprOrder` ends with the catch-all `| a, b => compare a.ctorIdx b.ctorIdx`, so a new `Resolved.Expr` constructor compiles without a same-constructor case and two different expressions of it compare as equal, which makes the clause order depend on insertion order. Fix: match on the first expression with one case for each constructor, and use the constructor-index fallback only in an inner match on the second expression.

The docstring of `Filter.accepts_atom` ("Folding preserves acceptance") does not restate the formula. Fix: say that for every argument list, expression and row, the filter of `atom` accepts the row exactly when the value of the expression in the bound context is truthy.

The proof sketch of `compileWhere_eq` still describes the removed proof ("simplify filtering by a constant decision"), but the proof now rewrites with `Filter.rows_eq` and `Filter.accepts_expr`. Fix: change the sketch to name these two laws as the strategy.
